title: DPIIT Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in Swachhata and Reduction of Pendency
subtitle:
Biomass Gasifier Installed at NCCBM’s Ballabgarh Campus to Promote Sustainable Waste-to-Energy Conversion
DPIIT Achieves 100% Disposal of Public Grievances Under Special Campaign 6, Reclaims 18,644 Sq. Ft. of Office Space
body_text: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), along with its attached and subordinate offices, concluded Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign, aimed at institutionalising the principles of Swachhata (cleanliness) and minimising pendency in official work, was undertaken across all offices to promote cleanliness, efficiency and effective record management. Special Campaign 6 was conducted from 2nd of October to 31st of October 2026, preceded by a preparatory phase from 15th of September to 30th September 2026. Throughout the campaign, DPIIT undertook focused efforts to promote awareness about cleanliness, systematic record management and the timely disposal of pending cases. With near-total achievement of the identified targets and notable progress across various campaign parameters, DPIIT reaffirmed its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, fostering a culture of efficiency and responsiveness, and strengthening sustainable practices in government functioning. As part of the campaign, the National Council for Cement and Building Materials (NCCBM), an autonomous organisation under DPIIT, installed a biomass gasifier at its Ballabgarh campus in Haryana. The gasifier uses biomass, wood and refuse-derived fuel (RDF) as feedstock to produce a combustible gas known as Syngas. During the campaign, NCCBM successfully conducted a trial run using 150 kg of dry horticultural waste. The waste was first shredded and subsequently converted into Syngas through partial oxidation at elevated temperatures under a controlled supply of gasifying agents. The potential utilisation of the Syngas generated through this process in power generation and diesel generator (DG) sets will be explored further. Trial runs using Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) obtained from Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) were also conducted in the gasifier during the campaign. This initiative showcases an environmentally sustainable approach to waste-to-energy conversion and offers a replicable model for promoting sustainable infrastructure, resource recovery and the principles of a circular economy. In addition to this initiative, DPIIT made significant progress across other key parameters of the campaign. Its attached and subordinate offices undertook the disposal of scrap materials and e-waste, resulting in the reclamation of 18,644 square feet of office space and the generation of ₹16,52,569 in revenue. The Department also achieved 100% completion in the disposal of public grievances and nearly 100% completion across other key parameters, including public grievance appeals, review of e-files and physical files, and cleanliness activities. Special attention was also given to improving the overall workplace environment to enhance employee comfort and productivity. These efforts reflect DPIIT's continued emphasis on accountability, efficient record management and the timely resolution of pending matters. *** Abhishek Dayal/ C N Abhijith Narayanan/ Abhimanyu Panwar
